scope: MEAS: independent source/order, bar map, gate arithmetic, fresh overlays and audio features (chroma transposition and lag tests, per-bar shift scan, vocal-range pitch ranking and traces, pitch-band onsets, audio-to-audio DTW against the other two Beach recordings); not aural review.

report.finding: The section matches results and checks: windows first [0.34, 0.40] and last [52.6, 52.9], no interior constraints, gates and score SHA-256 6eb0e709…5e6c. Config SHA-256 74b7432c… equals results.configSha256; the work candidate equals the public score; checks equal results; the pinned lc6212179.mxl and the cached audio match their SHA-256 values.

barMap.finding: All 995 notes lie inside their bar; bar times strictly increase; the first attack (the grace) is at 0.34 s and the last written hold ends at the −45 dB end, 54.52 s. The rasterised p1.svg shows D-flat major, 3/4, one opening clef/key/time group, the bar-1 grace and bars 1–29 with no repeat signs. Index and normalised SVG are identical to the 1908 and Gadski publications, and all three have identical note/bar identities.

independentChecks.tuningAndKey: librosa estimate −0.010 semitone = 439.75 Hz, equal to the published tuningHz. Rotating the audio chroma against the score chroma gives a mean framewise cosine of 0.749 at the written key, against ≤0.358 at ±1–3 semitones, so the recording is in D-flat as encoded.
independentChecks.lag: Global score/audio lag peaks at 0 s (0.749, against 0.711/0.704 at ∓0.25 s). In the per-bar ±2-s scan, 25 of 29 bars fit best within 0.3 s. The exceptions are bar 14 (+0.5 s, gain 0.01), bar 22 (+1.6 s, under the A-flat5 hold), bar 24 (−0.5 s) and bar 29 (−0.9 s, unchanged D-flat harmony).
independentChecks.voice: The written vocal pitch ranks first among MIDI 64–89 for 31 of 58 sung notes and in the top three for 41. Shifting the vocal line one note earlier or later at the same published times gives 11 or 15 firsts. Traces put C5 'morn' at 20.5–21.6 s (bar 13 at 20.484 s), the D-flat5 'lark's' entry at 22.3 s (published 22.473 s), D-flat5/E-flat5 in bar 15 at 23.5/24.0 s (23.552/24.060 s), the A-flat5 'right' hold from about 37.4 s (bar 22 at 37.100 s), G-flat5 'All's' at 41.8 s (41.764 s) and E-flat5 'right' at 42.6 s (bar 25 at 42.552 s).
independentChecks.endpoints: The bar-1 chord rises right after the grace placement (fresh 0–8.34 s overlay). D-flat5 'world' rises at 46.44–46.56 s (bar 26 at 46.544 s); the bar-28 rises are at 51.04/51.82 s (published 51.040/51.788 s); the final chord's D-flat6/F6/D-flat7 band rises 7.5 dB at 52.72 s (bar 29 at 52.736 s).
independentChecks.crossRecording: Audio-to-audio chroma DTW from this map into the Eames 1908 and Gadski recordings agrees with their independently published bar times within ±0.45 s for 24 and 23 of bars 1–26. The exceptions are a DTW start artefact at Gadski bar 1; bar 9, the 'pearled' rit. (+0.70 s in 1908); bar 23 (−0.46 s); and bar 14 (−1.25/−1.14 s). For bar 14 the vocal trace above confirms this map, and the 1908 and Gadski maps agree with each other (0.00 s). Bars 27–29 collapse in all DTW pairs, under the held D-flat harmony, and were checked by pitch bands instead.

overlays.finding: The fresh first-anchor overlay shows the grace placed immediately before the bar-1 chord rise at about 0.4 s and the bar 1–5 vocal and piano lines on the measured pitches. Results list this overlay. The REPORT's 0–12 and 36–56 s overlays were rendered after publication (04:57) but are not in the results list.

source.edition: OpenScore Lieder transcription of IMSLP #522898, D-flat major; printed imprint not established
source.structure: MEAS: 29 measures in each part, key −5 flats, 3/4 with bars 7 and 25 in 4/4, no repeat barlines; the lyrics give both settings of the opening lines (bars 1–9, 10–13) and then the lark/snail and 'God's in His heaven' lines (bars 14–28).

version.finding: The complete song is sung once in written order, in the encoded key. IMSLP #522898 is not opened here and is not claimed as Eames's performing copy.

limitations: MEAS: No aural review, build or browser run by RevScores. The initial D-flat2 grace is placed, not measured. Faint acoustic piano limits individual accompaniment-attack assurance; bar-level checks rely on vocal pitches and pitch bands.
